newsitem.title: USA: Full crude storage tanks depress U.S. cash crudes.
newsitem.headline: Full crude storage tanks depress U.S. cash crudes.

text.p: Full storage tanks in the U.S. Gulf continued to weigh on cash crude prices Monday, slightly deflating grade differentials as sweet and sour barrels attracted weaker offers in the face of heavy supplies.

Outright cash benchmark prices faltered as well, declining around 10 cents in line with NYMEX futures losses. July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late at $18.85-95 a barrel, some 20 cents firmer than July futures settlement at $18.68 a barrel due to strong Exchange for Physicals (EFPs).

EFP buyers are granted the option of exchanging their paper crude positions for a physical one, a move that has become extremely popular in the past two months due to uneconomical foreign crude deliveries against NYMEX matches.
EFPs were only quietly talked on Monday, but differentials ranged from +18 to 22 cents for July, and from +10 to 15 cents for August.
"From the way EFPs are holding-up in August it looks we'll have at least another month and a half of strong EFPs, until the foreign crudes find a refiner to run it," said a cash trader.

For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 25 cents under WTI/Cushing late in the session, pressured by weak Dated Brent prices and talk of a Brent cargo finding a home at WTI/Cushing minus 70-75 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland sold at discounts of $1.71 and $1.75, with Eugene Island firmly set below a $2.00 discount to the marker.
